caption: Figure 1 — Service map. Five client applications call six FastAPI services; three MongoDB databases hold identity, operations and accounting data respectively. The operational core, bill_service, is outlined in the accent colour.
Figure 2 — Request lifecycle for an authenticated write. Tenancy resolution precedes authorisation, and no query is built before both have succeeded.
Figure 3 — JWT issuance and tenancy resolution. The token is issued once, verified on every request, and is the sole carrier of laundry_id.
Figure 4 — Reference deployment topology: proxy at the edge, services on loopback, replica set and object storage behind a private network.
Figure 5 — Service dependency graph, drawn as a line diagram: authenticated HTTP between services, per-service credentials to each store.
Figure 6 — The tenancy decision chain. Each failure returns before the next check runs.
Figure 7 — Failure domains in the reference deployment: application host, database replica set, object storage.
Figure 8 — Envelope encryption at rest, with a separate deterministic path for equality search.
Figure 9 — Claim-by-claim comparison of staff and hotel client tokens.
Figure 10 — Laundry app sign-in with field annotations.
Figure 11 — Gate-pass register with annotations.
Figure 12 — Gate-pass editor, showing header fields and item lines.
Figure 13 — Day-close sequence, including the blocked branch when unbilled deliveries remain.
Figure 14 — Shop Counter today view.
Figure 15 — Quick bill pad: item list left, one-touch services and tender right.
Figure 16 — Hotel Desk overview for a single property.
Figure 17 — Request path from a client token to a scoped query, with the rejected paths shown.
Figure 18 — Linen state machine. Exceptions (mark_missing, mark_damaged, retire) branch from the active state.
Figure 19 — Scan station: scan field, current tag card and legal next actions.
Figure 20 — The linen state machine with its exception branches. Transitions are written by scan events only.
Figure 21 — Incident roles. In a small team one person may hold two roles, but the scribe role is never dropped.
Figure 22 — Severity bands with response targets and the people they summon.
Figure 23 — Backup, retention and point-in-time recovery timeline.
Figure 24 — Daily dumps, continuous oplog and the off-host copy, against the recovery-point target.
Figure 25 — Idempotent write path. The key and the record are committed together, so a crash cannot leave one without the other.
Figure 26 — Layered defences against double billing, from the data model to the day-close review.
Figure 27 — Test strategy pyramid: broad service-level coverage, thin top layer.
Figure 28 — Measured coverage by layer.
Figure 29 — Health dependency chain. The proxy routes only to services whose readiness probe passes.
Figure 30 — Maintenance calendar by cadence.
Figure 31 — Alert lifecycle and the escalation loop when acknowledgement does not happen within target.
